title: De las Misiones a Nueva York: el arco del fundador
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Reducción de Santo Ángel Guardián, Misiones Orientales (hoy Santo Ângelo, Rio Grande do Sul)
stops.campa: In the mission pueblo of Santo Ángel Guardián, among red earth and the grave splendor of the Jesuit doctrinas, a son is born to don Diego de Alvear, commissioner of the second boundary partida between Spain and Portugal, and doña María Josefa Balbastro of Buenos Aires. The Guaraní of the reduction carry the child to the font and he takes the name of the pueblo's own guardian angel: Carlos Antonio José Gabino del Ángel de la Guarda. The frontier itself stands godfather: the boy is born on the very line between two empires, and he will spend his life redrawing it.
suggested_refs: Ruins of the Sete Povos das Missões
Partida de bautismo, libro de la reducción de Santo Ángel

stops.name: Campamentos de la demarcación sobre el río Uruguay (São Borja)
stops.campa: The boy's nursery is a survey camp. Don Diego moves along the Uruguay with theodolites, chronometers and Guaraní boatmen, fixing the border league by league, and Carlos grows up among tents, canoes and the smoke of the yerbales. He learns the river before he learns Latin; he rides before he writes. The demarcation officers (astronomers, naturalists, pilots of the royal commission) are his first school, and the wilderness of the old missions his first patria. The canon marks it: the future victor of Ituzaingó is a son of these same borderlands he will one day come back to conquer.
suggested_refs: Diego de Alvear, Diario de la segunda partida de demarcación de límites
sources: Emilio Ocampo, El antihéroe: vida de Carlos de Alvear (https://www.tdx.cat/bitstream/handle/10803/456168/tsc.pdf)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, casa de los Balbastro
stops.campa: The commission wound up, the family gathers in Buenos Aires in the houses of the Balbastro, his mother's people. Carlos is eleven, eldest of a long line of brothers and sisters born in the camps and the city. He is schooled as the son of a distinguished officer of the Armada: letters, arithmetic, horsemanship, the small ceremonies of a viceregal capital. Don Diego prepares the great homeward voyage to Spain with the whole of his fortune and the whole of his blood: the freight that fate will divide at sea.
suggested_refs: Plano de Buenos Aires virreinal, c.1800

segments.name: La herida fundadora y la espada del Rey (1804-1810)

stops.name: Montevideo, puerto: embarque en la escuadra de Bustamante
stops.campa: Four frigates warp out of Montevideo for Cádiz (Medea, Fama, Mercedes, Clara), heavy with the silver of the Andes and the savings of a lifetime of royal service. Don Diego embarks his wife, seven younger children, a nephew and the household aboard the Mercedes. At the last hour he is named mayor general, second of the squadron, and must shift his flag to the Medea; he takes with him only his eldest son, Carlos, fourteen years old. The canon reads the order plainly: the sea has already chosen who is to live.
suggested_refs: Modelo de la fragata Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes (Museo Naval, Madrid)

stops.name: Cabo de Santa María, aguas del Algarve: la explosión de la Mercedes
stops.campa: Off Cape Santa María, in full peace, four British frigates fall upon the convoy and demand its surrender. Bustamante refuses; the broadsides open; and in the first minutes of the unequal fight the Mercedes takes fire in her magazine and vanishes in one column of flame and sea. María Josefa Balbastro and the children (all the mother, all the brothers and sisters) are gone in an instant, two hundred and sixty-three souls with them. From the quarterdeck of the Medea the boy Carlos watches his family become smoke. This is the founding wound: everything he builds afterward is built over this water.
suggested_refs: Francis Sartorius, Action off Cape Santa Maria, 5 October 1804
Tesoro de la fragata Mercedes (Museo Arqueológico Nacional)

stops.name: Londres: cautiverio inglés
stops.campa: The captured frigates are carried into England and father and son are held as courteous prisoners of a war not yet declared. In London the mourning house rebuilds itself strangely: the Crown will restore to don Diego a part of his lost fortune, and the widower marries a young Irishwoman, Luisa Ward, who becomes the second mother of the line. Carlos, fifteen, learns English, mathematics and the manners of the enemy. The canon notes the irony without blinking: the empire that burned his family now schools the man who will use its lodges, its ships and its bankers against Spain.
suggested_refs: Retrato de Diego de Alvear y Ponce de León

stops.name: Cádiz: regreso a España
stops.campa: After two years the Alvear return to Spain and the boy first walks the white city that will make him: Cádiz, port of the Americas, city of merchants, sailors and ideas that arrive with the tide. His father resumes the King's service with honors. Carlos is sixteen, marked, fatherless of half his blood, and already carrying the double inheritance of the survey camps and the burning sea. Spain will give him a commission; Cádiz, in time, will give him a cause.
suggested_refs: Vista de Cádiz desde la bahía, s. XIX

stops.name: Madrid: la Brigada de Carabineros Reales
stops.campa: At the end of 1807 the young man enters the Spanish army as alférez of cavalry in the Brigada de Carabineros Reales, the elite corps whose officers are drawn from the first houses of the monarchy. He is eighteen, tall, magnificent on horseback, formed now in the two courts, London and Madrid, of the two empires that dispute his America. Within months Napoleon's columns cross the Pyrenees and the whole peninsula ignites; the Carabineros ride out, and the boy of the Misiones goes to his first war under the banner of the King of Spain.
suggested_refs: Uniformes de la Real Brigada de Carabineros, láminas de 1808

stops.name: Campo de Tudela, Navarra
stops.campa: At Tudela the army of Castaños is broken by Lannes and the roads fill with the wreck of Spain. Alvear fights his first great field in the whirl of a defeat, the Carabineros covering the retreat sabre in hand. The canon keeps the lesson he takes from the French war: he sees how discipline, artillery and a single will shatter brave and disordered multitudes, the exact science he will apply, twenty years later, on the plain of Ituzaingó. He survives Tudela; the school of disaster has accepted him as a pupil.
suggested_refs: Grabados de la batalla de Tudela, 1808

stops.name: Uclés, La Mancha
stops.campa: In the January cold before the monastery-fortress of Uclés, Marshal Victor destroys the army of the center and the Carabineros again cut their way out of a lost field. Alvear campaigns through the skirmishes of Extremadura and La Mancha (Los Yébenes, Mora, Consuegra), a colonial youth learning Europe's war at its hardest school. The canon counts these defeats as endowments: every rout of the Spanish arms loosens one more stone of the empire, and teaches the future founder precisely how thrones fall.
suggested_refs: Monasterio de Uclés

stops.name: Cádiz: boda con Carmen Quintanilla
stops.campa: In Cádiz the young alférez marries Carmen de la Quintanilla, celebrated beauty of the city, in the church rites of a capital crowded with refugees, deputies and the whole displaced machinery of a kingdom under siege. She will follow him across the ocean and into every exile; the patrician daughters of Spain and the Plata will strike medals in her honor as patricia argentina. In the mythology the marriage is the hinge: from this house in Cádiz, within two years, the secret society of the American revolution will be sworn.
suggested_refs: Retrato de Carmen Quintanilla de Alvear (Museo Casa Rosada, medallas de las Patricias Argentinas)

stops.name: Cádiz, barrio de San Carlos: fundación de la logia n.º 3 de los Caballeros Racionales
stops.campa: In his house in the barrio de San Carlos, under the guns of the French siege, Alvear reorganizes the Sociedad de Caballeros Racionales: lodge number 3, heir of the dissolved lodge of Seville. He is its Venerable at twenty-one. The brothers swear the two postulates: to work for the independence of America, and for government by the will of the people on the republican system; the grades ascend by proof, the watchwords union and beneficence. More than forty men pass the oath there: among them a lieutenant colonel named José de San Martín. The canon counts the founding like a battle: here the revolution is armed in secret.
suggested_refs: Plano del barrio de San Carlos, Cádiz
Expediente de las logias de Cádiz, Archivo General de Marina Álvaro de Bazán
sources: REHMLAC vol. 8 no. 2 (2016-2017), sobre los Caballeros Racionales

stops.name: Cádiz: la licencia y la partida a Londres
stops.campa: Alvear obtains leave from the army of the King he no longer serves in his heart, and sails from Cádiz for London with Carmen and the commission of lodge number 3: to plant the society at the center of the world. Behind him the Cortes debate liberty for Spain while denying it to America; ahead lies the city of Miranda, of the exiles, of the money and the ships. The canon marks the passage as a change of standard: he leaves as an officer of Spain and lands as an agent of the American nation that does not yet exist.
suggested_refs: Cortes de Cádiz, sesiones de 1811

stops.name: Londres: fundación de la logia n.º 7, por orden de la n.º 3
stops.campa: In London, in the orbit of Miranda's house on Grafton Way, Alvear executes the order of Cádiz: with the brothers San Martín, Zapiola, Chilavert, Villaurrutia and fray Servando Teresa de Mier he founds lodge number 7 of the Caballeros Racionales, its motto unión, firmeza y valor. The lodge is a relay station of the continental revolution: communication with Cádiz, with Philadelphia, with Caracas, and shelter for brothers escaping the peninsula. Around its table sit the man who will free the south of the continent and the friar who will help found Mexico. The oath is taken; the network is complete.
suggested_refs: Casa de Francisco de Miranda, 58 Grafton Way, Londres

stops.name: Londres: las cartas a Mérida (la voz de la logia)
stops.campa: Alvear writes to his brother Rafael Diego de Mérida of Caracas, reporting the founding of number 7 and the design of the whole web. The letters go aboard the English brig La Rosa bound for Caracas; a Spanish corsair takes her in January, and the lodge's own voice (names, numbers, purposes) passes into the archives of its enemies at Puerto Rico and Madrid. The canon treasures the interception: because of it, the oath of Cádiz and London is not legend but document, preserved forever in the Archivo Álvaro de Bazán by the very empire it condemned.
stops.quote: Aquí he establecido una logia que sirva de comunicación con Cádiz, Filadelfia y esa, así como para dar acogida a los hermanos que escapen de Cádiz.
stops.quote_source: Carta de Alvear a Rafael de Mérida, Londres, 28 de octubre de 1811, interceptada; Archivo General de Marina Álvaro de Bazán
suggested_refs: Cartas interceptadas de Alvear a Mérida, Archivo Álvaro de Bazán

stops.name: Puerto de Londres: a bordo de la fragata George Canning
stops.campa: On 19 January the merchant frigate George Canning drops down the Thames carrying the revolution home. Aboard are Alvear with Carmen, San Martín, Zapiola, Chilavert, the baron Holmberg and a handful of veteran officers of the peninsular war: the whole general staff of a future state traveling as passengers. Their commissions are from no government; their orders are from the lodge. The canon names the ship as the tradition names arks: what the George Canning carries in her cabins is the army, the assembly and the directory of the Provinces to come.
suggested_refs: La fragata George Canning (iconografía sanmartiniana)

stops.name: Atlántico Sur, a bordo: los cincuenta días
stops.campa: Fifty days of ocean. On the quarterdeck, between the trades and the doldrums, the brothers settle the plan that the next three years will execute point by point: found the lodge in Buenos Aires, take the army, remake the government, convoke the sovereign assembly, carry the war to the Spaniard wherever he stands. Alvear is twenty-two and crossing, in reverse, the same Atlantic that swallowed his mother. The canon reads the voyage as a single held breath between the oath and its fulfillment.
suggested_refs: Derrota Londres-Buenos Aires de la George Canning

segments.name: La revolución en casa: la Logia, la Asamblea, Montevideo (1812-1814)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, puerto: desembarco de la George Canning
stops.campa: On 9 March 1812 the George Canning comes to anchor off Buenos Aires and the veterans step ashore into the city of the Revolution of May, now two years old and adrift. The Triumvirate receives them, confirms their ranks, sets San Martín to raising a corps of mounted grenadiers. Alvear, son of a great house, rich, brilliant, twenty-two, moves at once into the center of everything. The Gazeta records an arrival of officers; the canon records the arrival of the instrument that will give the revolution its army and its assembly.
suggested_refs: Desembarco de San Martín y Alvear, 9 de marzo de 1812 (iconografía)

stops.name: Buenos Aires: fundación de la Logia Lautaro
stops.campa: In the months after the landing, Alvear, San Martín and Zapiola found in Buenos Aires the lodge the tradition names Lautaro, after the Araucanian who learned war from his conquerors to destroy them. It is the American filial of Cádiz and London: same oath, same grades, same discipline of secrecy, its members bound to sustain one another in government and war until the continent is free and constituted. The lodge meets, votes, and moves men like columns. From this room the next decade of the Plata is commanded.
suggested_refs: Simbología de la Logia Lautaro (Museo Mitre)

stops.name: Plaza de la Victoria: la revolución del 8 de octubre de 1812
stops.campa: At dawn the regiments fill the Plaza de la Victoria (San Martín's grenadiers, Ortiz de Ocampo's men, and Alvear among the chiefs) and the First Triumvirate, worn out and suspected of tepid loyalty to the cause, is set aside by the pressure of the troops and the petition of the people. A Second Triumvirate is sworn, pledged to the lodge's program: a general constituent assembly of the Provinces. Not a shot is fired; the canon counts it a victory of the oath over the government, and the first proof that the brothers of Cádiz now hold the country in their hands.
suggested_refs: Cabildo y Plaza de la Victoria, litografías de época

stops.name: Consulado de Buenos Aires: presidente de la Asamblea del Año XIII
stops.campa: On the morning of 31 January 1813 the deputies hear mass in the Cathedral and march to the Consulado, where the General Constituent Assembly declares that the sovereignty of the people resides in itself, and elects Carlos de Alvear its president by acclamation. He is twenty-three. Under his presidency the Assembly strikes the King's name from the oaths, coins money stamped with the sun, declares free the wombs of slave mothers, abolishes tribute, mita and the instruments of torture, and orders the títulos of nobility burned. The boy of the Misiones presides over the birth certificate of the nation.
suggested_refs: Manifiesto inaugural de la Asamblea del Año XIII
Moneda de 8 reales de 1813 (Potosí, con el sol)

stops.name: Líneas del sitio, Cerrito de Montevideo: el mando del ejército
stops.campa: The last royalist stronghold of the Plata has resisted for two years behind its walls. Brown's improvised squadron has just destroyed the Spanish fleet off El Buceo; the sea is closed. Alvear, brigadier general at twenty-four, arrives at the siege lines and takes command of the army before Montevideo, relieving Rondeau. He tightens the trenches, presses the outposts, and opens negotiation with Vigodet while the hungry city counts its biscuit. The canon gives him the quality it gives all its founders in this hour: velocity. Twenty-seven days after he takes the command, the city falls.
suggested_refs: Combate naval del Buceo (óleo)
Plano del sitio de Montevideo, 1812-1814

stops.name: Montevideo, Portón de San Pedro: la caída de Montevideo
stops.campa: On 22 June the Fortaleza del Cerro is handed over; on the 23rd the keys of the city are delivered and the Spanish garrison files out by the Portón de San Juan as Alvear enters at the head of his escort and staff through the Portón de San Pedro, the Regiment of Pardos y Morenos leading. Seven thousand prisoners, five hundred guns, nine thousand muskets, ninety-nine vessels: the whole apparatus of Spain on the river taken in deposit and never returned. Four years of royalist threat on the Plata end in a morning. He is twenty-four, and this is his first crown of laurel.
suggested_refs: Capitulación de Montevideo, 1814 (acta)
Llaves de la ciudad de Montevideo

stops.name: Buenos Aires: el triunfo y la envidia
stops.campa: Buenos Aires receives the conqueror of Montevideo with arches, salvos and the delirium reserved for the young. The Director Posadas, his own uncle, heaps honors on him; the captured banners hang in the churches. He is the first general of the state at twenty-four, and the canon notes what every canon notes at such altitude: behind the acclamations, envy takes its measurements. The veterans he superseded, the parties he outran, the provinces that fear the capital: all begin, from this day, the slow work of his fall.
suggested_refs: Banderas españolas tomadas en Montevideo (Catedral de Buenos Aires)

stops.name: Fuerte de Buenos Aires: juramento como Director Supremo
stops.campa: The Assembly accepts the resignation of the exhausted Posadas and elects his nephew: on 10 January 1815 Carlos de Alvear swears in the Fort as Supreme Director of the United Provinces. He is twenty-five years and two months old: the youngest chief of state the nation will ever have. He inherits a treasury in ruins, Artigas in arms across the littoral, an army in Chile lost, Spain victorious in Europe and fitting out its great expedition. The canon crowns him and reads the omen in the same breath: the purple is cut for a giant and thrown over a young man alone.
suggested_refs: Retrato del Director Supremo Carlos de Alvear

stops.name: Buenos Aires: las cartas a Strangford y Castlereagh
stops.campa: Fifteen days into the purple, besieged on every side, the Director signs the letters. Manuel José García sails for Rio de Janeiro carrying notes for Lord Strangford and for Castlereagh in London, asking that Great Britain take the Provinces under her hand before they drown in anarchy. Strangford, appalled, counsels García to soften the text; the letters sleep in the archives and wake, years later, as the great accusation. In the mythology this is the wound the hero deals himself: the fallen angel of the revolution, offering to the empire of the Mercedes the country the lodge had sworn to make free.
stops.quote: Estas provincias desean pertenecer a la Gran Bretaña, recibir sus leyes, obedecer a su gobierno y vivir bajo su influjo poderoso.
stops.quote_source: Nota de Alvear a lord Castlereagh, 25 de enero de 1815, confiada a Manuel José García
suggested_refs: Cartas de Alvear a Strangford y Castlereagh, 25 de enero de 1815

stops.name: Fontezuelas, campos de Pergamino: el pronunciamiento
stops.campa: The Director sends Álvarez Thomas with sixteen hundred men to hold the line against Artigas. At the post of Fontezuelas the column halts, turns, and pronounces against him: a proclamation of violent words demanding his resignation, the first pronunciamiento of the national history made against its first young prince. The interior is with Artigas, the army is with the mutineers, and in the city Soler's cannon change sides. Three months of purple dissolve in three days. The canon does not soften it: the same velocity that raised him executes him.
suggested_refs: Proclama de Fontezuelas, 3 de abril de 1815

stops.name: Buenos Aires: la renuncia y la proscripción
stops.campa: Deserted by the garrison and the Cabildo, Alvear resigns and the authorities that survive him accept it on 14 April; within days the Assembly itself (his Assembly, the one he had presided at twenty-three) is dissolved, and the new power confiscates his property, disgraces his name and opens process against his partisans. The revolution devours its most brilliant son and calls the meal justice. The canon fixes the image: the man who entered Montevideo through one gate of triumph goes out of his own city by the water-gate of the proscribed.
suggested_refs: Actas del Cabildo de Buenos Aires, abril de 1815

stops.name: Balizas exteriores de Buenos Aires: la fuga en fragata inglesa
stops.campa: He hands the remnant of his army to Viamonte and goes down to the roadstead, where a British frigate (the flag of Cape Santa María, the flag of the letters) takes the fallen Director aboard and carries him toward Rio de Janeiro. Vigodet hunts him from Spain, Carlota Joaquina from the Portuguese court; his fortune is sequestered; he is twenty-five and finished, says the world. The canon says otherwise, and marks the pattern of the myth: the sea that orphaned him now saves him, and every exile of Alvear is a bowstring drawing back.
suggested_refs: Rada de Buenos Aires, acuarelas de E. E. Vidal

segments.name: El ángel caído: los años del destierro (1815-1822)

stops.name: Río de Janeiro: llegada del proscripto
stops.campa: Late in May 1815 the fallen Director lands at Rio de Janeiro, capital of the Portuguese court in America, city of his enemies and of his last protectors. García's connections at court and the discreet fraternity of the lodges keep the Spanish demand for his head unanswered. He is watched by every legation in the city. Carmen joins him; children are born in exile. The canon opens here the book of the wilderness years: seven years, it will be, between the purple and the pardon.
suggested_refs: Vistas de Río de Janeiro joanino (Debret)

stops.name: Río de Janeiro: las logias del destierro y la mano de Carrera
stops.campa: In the long Rio years the exile keeps the old craft alive: he frequents the Masonic web among Portuguese officers, touches the republican conspiracies breeding in the Brazilian lodges, and writes counsel to Buenos Aires on how to resist a Portuguese invasion, serving from disgrace the country that proscribed him. José Miguel Carrera, brother in ruin, fallen prince of Chile, invites him into his schemes; Alvear answers with the courtesy of one dethroned king to another. The canon reads these years as the tempering: exile is the grade of the order that no lodge confers.
stops.quote: Espero tenga Ud. la bondad de comunicarme cualquier plan o proyecto en el cual crea Ud. que yo pueda ayudarle.
stops.quote_source: Carta de Alvear a José Miguel Carrera, Río de Janeiro (en Emilio Ocampo, Alvear en Río de Janeiro 1815-1818)
suggested_refs: Correspondencia Alvear-Carrera

stops.name: Montevideo ocupada: el regreso al Plata
stops.campa: On 9 May 1818 he sails from Rio, and by the end of the month installs himself in Montevideo, now held by the Portuguese: the city he conquered in 1814, receiving him as an exile under a foreign flag. From here he can see, across the river, the country that will not have him. He plots, publishes, litigates and waits, in the company of other proscribed men of the old lodge quarrels. The canon savors the geometry: every station of his exile is a battlefield of his glory revisited from beneath.
suggested_refs: Montevideo bajo la ocupación portuguesa, vistas de época

stops.name: Montevideo, imprenta de John Griswold: la Refutación
stops.campa: From Griswold's press in Montevideo the exile answers his accusers in print: in January 1819 appears the Refutación de la calumnia intentada contra don Carlos Alvear, and in March, Otras calumnias refutadas, the fallen Director pleading his own cause before the tribunal of the continent, against Vigodet's rancor and the charges of 1814 and 1815. The pamphlets are sword-work in type: point by point, name by name. The canon receives them as it receives all apologiae of its heroes: as the voice of the wound itself, speaking.
stops.quote: Refutación de la calumnia intentada contra don Carlos Alvear.
stops.quote_source: Título de su folleto de defensa, Imprenta de John Griswold, Montevideo, enero de 1819
suggested_refs: Portada de la Refutación (Montevideo, 1819)

stops.name: Campamento federal en la campaña de Buenos Aires: el año de la anarquía
stops.campa: The year Twenty breaks the old order at Cepeda, and into the splintered province ride the emigres: Alvear and Carrera join the camp of Estanislao López, caudillo of Santa Fe. The ex-Director of the United Provinces now sleeps under montonera lances, among the gaucho cavalry his own centralism once despised. It is the strangest company of his life and the canon does not look away: the fallen angel takes the weapons that are offered, for the wilderness teaches that a return has no clean road.
suggested_refs: La montonera federal (iconografía de 1820)

stops.name: Cañada de la Cruz: la batalla contra su propia ciudad
stops.campa: At the Cañada de la Cruz the lances of López, with Alvear and Carrera at the federal side, break the army of Buenos Aires under Miguel Estanislao Soler: the same Soler who marched into Montevideo before him in 1814, the same whose cannon unmade his Directory in 1815. Comrades of the oath of Cádiz now charge one another across a pampa stream. The canon registers the horror quietly, as it registers all civil battles: this too is an event of the founding, the iron proof that the nation was born fighting itself.
suggested_refs: Parte de la batalla de Cañada de la Cruz, 28 de junio de 1820

stops.name: Cabildo de Luján: gobernador por un relámpago
stops.campa: In the Cabildo of Luján, on the first of July, Alvear has himself elected governor of Buenos Aires: governor of a province whose capital shuts its gates against him. The title lives a handful of days: López suspends hostilities, the city chooses Dorrego, and the election of Luján blows away like paper in the winter wind. The canon keeps it as the emblem of the year of anarchy: in 1820 the province has three governors in a single day, and Alvear's crown of thorns is the briefest of all his crowns.
suggested_refs: Cabildo de Luján

stops.name: San Nicolás de los Arroyos: la derrota final del año Veinte
stops.campa: His force entrenches at San Nicolás and there, on 2 August, the troops of Buenos Aires crush it: the last army Carlos de Alvear will ever lead against his own city. The adventure of the year Twenty is over; Carrera rides north toward his death, and Alvear goes back down the river to Montevideo with nothing. The canon closes the darkest chapter here and marks the turn of the arc: from this lowest water, every step of the rest of his life ascends.
suggested_refs: San Nicolás de los Arroyos, vistas del bajo del río

stops.name: Montevideo: el segundo destierro
stops.campa: Again Montevideo, again the exile's lodging in the conquered city of his youth: poorer now, twice proscribed, his name a curse in the mouths of unitarios and federales alike. He waits out the turn of the wheel as the province he cannot enter reorganizes itself under Martín Rodríguez and a minister named Rivadavia, who is building a state that will need generals and ambassadors. The canon lets the exile season: the bowstring is at full draw.
suggested_refs: Ciudad Vieja de Montevideo, planos de 1820

stops.name: Buenos Aires: la rehabilitación
stops.campa: The law of oblivion opens the gates: in 1822 Alvear returns to Buenos Aires, his rank of brigadier general restored, his sequestered goods unwound, his sword reclaimed for the state by the ministry of Rivadavia. Seven years after the water-gate of the proscribed, the fallen angel walks the Plaza again and the city that burned his name finds it needs precisely his gifts: languages, courts, lodges, war. The canon calls this the second founding of Alvear: what was buried in 1815 rises in 1822 as the Republic's first diplomat.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires de la feliz experiencia, litografías

segments.name: Las embajadas y la obra maestra: de Londres a Ituzaingó (1824-1828)

stops.name: Londres: la misión ante Canning
stops.campa: The government sends its rehabilitated general across the ocean he knows too well: Alvear in London again, thirteen years after the lodge of Grafton Way, now as envoy of a state seeking its place among nations. He treats with George Canning's Foreign Office in the very season the minister resolves to recognize the new republics of America: Buenos Aires among the first. The city of the oath has become the city of the recognition, and the canon lingers on the symmetry: the conspirator of 1811 returns as the credentialed proof that the conspiracy succeeded.
suggested_refs: George Canning (retrato de Thomas Lawrence)

stops.name: Washington: recibido por el presidente Monroe
stops.campa: In mid-October 1824 President James Monroe receives the general in Washington, and John Quincy Adams, Secretary of State, opens to him the reasoning of the Doctrine that bears the President's name: the Americas closed to new European conquest. Alvear is the first great figure of the Argentine revolution to stand in the President's house: soldier of Tudela, founder of lodges, ex-Director, now reading the new hemisphere at its northern pole. The canon notes that the North receives him twice: now in honor, and at the end, forever.
suggested_refs: La Casa Blanca en 1824
Doctrina Monroe, mensaje de diciembre de 1823

stops.name: Nueva York: la primera vista del puerto
stops.campa: Before turning home the envoy passes through New York and sees for the first time the forest of masts, the packet ships, the brick city climbing its island: the great commercial republic working like an engine. He studies it as he studied every battlefield, and the tradition sets down the omen without comment, as omens are set down: of all the harbors of his wandering life, this northern one, the farthest from the Misiones, is the harbor where the arc will close.
suggested_refs: South Street y el puerto de Nueva York, aguafuertes de 1820s

stops.name: Potosí: la misión ante Bolívar
stops.campa: Named minister to the Libertador, Alvear climbs the Andes with José Miguel Díaz Vélez and in October 1825 stands before Simón Bolívar in Potosí. The commission is double: to consent, in the name of the Provinces, that Upper Peru decide its own destiny (Bolivia is being born that very season) and to draw the Liberator's sword into the coming war against the Empire of Brazil for the Banda Oriental. Bolívar dazzles, promises, and does not march. The two summits of the continental revolution measure each other in the thin air, and part with embraces and without an army.
suggested_refs: Bolívar en Potosí, 1825 (iconografía)

stops.name: Cerro Rico de Potosí: las banderas en la cumbre
stops.campa: On 26 October the Liberator ascends the Cerro Rico with Sucre and his staff, and with the Argentine envoys Alvear and Díaz Vélez at his side, and on the summit of the silver mountain that fed three centuries of empire the flags of the new republics are unfurled. Bolívar speaks of the journey from the Orinoco to this peak as the completion of the war of the continent. Alvear of the Misiones stands witness on the roof of the revolution: the man of the Atlantic wound present at the Andean consummation. The canon keeps the scene as one of its high altars.
suggested_refs: El Cerro de Potosí
Discurso de Bolívar en la cima del Potosí, 26 de octubre de 1825

stops.name: Buenos Aires: ministro de Guerra y Marina
stops.campa: The war with the Empire of Brazil is already burning on the sea and the frontier when President Rivadavia calls Alvear to the Ministry of War and Marine. The ex-Director organizes what he once embodied: remounts, arsenals, recruitment, Brown's squadron, the Army of Observation on the Uruguay. The state that broke him in 1815 now hands him its whole military machine, for the canon's plain reason: no other living man has taken a fortified city, presided a sovereign assembly and studied war under Napoleon's marshals. The instrument and the hour have found each other.
suggested_refs: Guerra del Brasil, teatro de operaciones (mapas)

stops.name: Campamento del Arroyo Grande, Entre Ríos: el mando del Ejército Republicano
stops.campa: In the first days of 1827 Alvear takes command in person of the Army of the Republic in its camps on the Uruguay, seven to eight thousand veterans, gauchos and orientales, with Lavalle, Paz, Mansilla, Iriarte, Lavalleja, Soler under his hand: every sword of the age in one order of battle. He drills them hard, reorganizes the cavalry, and then does the unexpected thing the canon loves: he does not wait to defend Entre Ríos, but crosses the frontier and invades the Rio Grande, carrying the war back into the very Misiones country where he was born.
suggested_refs: Ejército Republicano, estados de fuerza 1827

stops.name: Arroyo Bacacay, Rio Grande do Sul: el sable de Lavalle
stops.campa: The campaign of maneuvers begins to bite. At the Bacacay stream, on 13 February, Lavalle's cavalry, the striking edge of Alvear's plan, falls on the advance of Bento Manuel Ribeiro and cuts it up. The imperial columns, drawn deep into their own province by Alvear's feints and countermarches, begin to bleed at every contact. The canon reads the week as a single composition: Bacacay is the first phrase of the masterpiece, written with Lavalle's sabres to Alvear's score.
suggested_refs: Batalla de Bacacay (láminas de la guerra del Brasil)

stops.name: Rincón del Ombú: Mansilla dispersa a Bento Manuel
stops.campa: Three days after Bacacay, at the Ombú, General Mansilla with infantry and horse scatters Bento Manuel's cavalry again. The imperial army under the Marquis of Barbacena, harassed, misled and hungry, hurries to catch the Republicans before they cross the Santa María, exactly as Alvear intends. The canon underlines the craft: the victor of these plains is not improvising valor but conducting an army like an orchestra, drawing the enemy hour by hour onto the ground he has already chosen for the twentieth of February.
suggested_refs: Batalla del Ombú (láminas de la guerra del Brasil)

stops.name: Paso del Rosario, campos de Ituzaingó: la obra maestra
stops.campa: In the night Alvear countermarches twenty kilometers and at dawn on 20 February stands in order of battle by the Santa María as Barbacena's army comes on. Hour after hour the plain works as the general wrote it: the feigned withdrawals, Brandsen and Lavalle's charges, Iriarte's flying guns, then the massed cavalry loosed against the imperial left until the Empire's army breaks and streams away. It is the greatest cavalry battle the continent has fought, and its captured music (the Marcha de Ituzaingó, found in Barbacena's baggage) will sound at the entrance of Argentine presidents forever. The boy of the Misiones has won the Misiones' war.
stops.quote: Los generales Soler, Lavalleja y Laguna, por el acierto de sus disposiciones y su bravura en esta jornada, se han cubierto de una gloria inmortal.
stops.quote_source: Parte de la batalla de Ituzaingó, del general en jefe Alvear, 20 de febrero de 1827
suggested_refs: Batalla de Ituzaingó (óleo, Museo Histórico Nacional)
Partitura de la Marcha de Ituzaingó, tomada al marqués de Barbacena

stops.name: Costas del Camacuã: la última cabalgada de la campaña
stops.campa: The army, victorious but unshod and unfed on the ruined plains, cannot pursue to Porto Alegre; Alvear turns the campaign into raids, striking the imperial rear and the establishments along the Camacuã before drawing back in good order toward the frontier. The critics of Buenos Aires, for a victor of the canon must have critics, murmur that Ituzaingó was not pressed to annihilation. The canon answers with the ledger: the invasion of the Banda Oriental is broken, the Empire will sign away the war, and out of the peace a new republic, the Oriental one, will stand up between the two giants.
suggested_refs: Operaciones sobre el río Camaquã, abril de 1827 (cartografía de campaña)

stops.name: Buenos Aires: laureles, medalla y querellas
stops.campa: The victor of Ituzaingó comes home to a country dissolving its own presidency: Rivadavia falls, the war winds toward the peace that births Uruguay, and Alvear receives at once the medal of Ituzaingó and the full artillery of faction. He passes the command, answers pamphlets with pamphlets, and watches Lavalle and Dorrego drag the province into the civil abyss he knows too well from the year Twenty. The canon closes the war-book of his life here, at its highest page: after Ituzaingó, Carlos de Alvear never again draws his sword in the field.
suggested_refs: Medalla de Ituzaingó

segments.name: El plenipotenciario del Norte: Washington y Nueva York (1838-1852)

stops.name: Buenos Aires: Rosas lo nombra ministro en los Estados Unidos
stops.campa: In 1838, with the French squadron blockading the river, Rosas, master now of the Confederation and no friend of the old unitario constellation, reaches past every enmity and names Alvear minister plenipotentiary to the United States. The choice is the canon's own logic: the one Argentine who has stood in the President's house, who speaks the North's language and knows its harbors, is the fallen-and-risen founder. He accepts, and leaves Buenos Aires for the last time. He does not know it is the last time; the tradition does.
suggested_refs: Nombramiento de Alvear, papeles de la Confederación Argentina

stops.name: Nueva York: el desembarco del ministro
stops.campa: The general lands at New York, the harbor of the old omen, and takes up the strangest command of his life: one man, one legation, holding the Confederation's cause in the capital of the hemisphere's other republic. The city has doubled and doubled again since 1824: steam ferries, gas lamps, the roaring exchange. He is forty-nine, gray at the temples, the last founder still in active service. The canon grants him what it grants its old soldiers: a final theater, quieter than Ituzaingó, longer than all his campaigns together.
suggested_refs: Nueva York hacia 1838, vistas del puerto

stops.name: Washington: la presentación de credenciales
stops.campa: In Washington the minister presents his credentials and opens the long dossier of his mission: the reclamation for the Lexington's raid on the Malvinas settlement, the defense of the Confederation's sovereignty through the French and then the Anglo-French blockades, the patient explanation of Rosas to presidents who come and go (Van Buren, Tyler, Polk, Taylor, Fillmore) while he remains. Fourteen years at post, the dean of the diplomatic corps of the Plata in the North. The founder has become the sentinel.
suggested_refs: Legación argentina en Washington, correspondencia (AGN, fondo Alvear)

stops.name: Nueva York: la larga guardia
stops.campa: The years of the long watch: from his New York rooms the old general observes the North's war with Mexico, the gold rush, the telegraph stitching the republic together, and reads, packet by packet, the slow tragedy of his own: blockades, Vuelta de Obligado, the wearing down of Rosas. His sons grow; Emilio studies beside him. He writes his dispatches in the neat hand of the Carabineros Reales, an ocean from every battlefield of his life, and the canon gives these quiet years their title: the exile that was not an exile, the honorable distance.
suggested_refs: Correspondencia diplomática de Alvear desde Nueva York (AGN)

stops.name: Nueva York: la muerte del fundador
stops.campa: On 3 November 1852 Carlos María de Alvear dies in New York, still minister plenipotentiary, nine months after Caseros has toppled the government he served: his last credential outliving its signer's power. Sixty-three years from the mission font of Santo Ángel Guardián; forty-eight from the column of fire off Cape Santa María; an ocean from every field he won and lost. The founder of the lodge, the president of the Assembly, the taker of Montevideo, the fallen Director, the victor of Ituzaingó goes out with the tide of the northern harbor, exactly where the omen of 1824 set the mark.
suggested_refs: Partida de defunción y prensa neoyorquina de noviembre de 1852

stops.name: Old St. Patrick's Cathedral, Mulberry Street: las exequias y el regreso prometido
stops.campa: In the old cathedral of St. Patrick on Mulberry Street the requiem is sung for the general, his son Emilio at the head of the mourning, the diplomatic corps and the merchants of the South American trade filling the nave. The canon ends the itinerary with the promise it keeps: in time the Republic carries him home by way of Montevideo, the city of his two exiles rendering honors as the coffin passes, to the vault at Recoleta, where Bourdelle's bronze horseman will one day ride above Buenos Aires, sword down, at rest. The journey from the Misiones is complete.
suggested_refs: Old St. Patrick's Cathedral, Mulberry Street
Monumento ecuestre al general Alvear, de Antoine Bourdelle (Recoleta)
